---
title: "Extracting a row or a column drops a dimension"
ref: IDX-01
categories: [Indexing]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'is.matrix(matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)[1, ])'
reponse: 'FALSE'
attendu: "a one-row matrix, and a one-column data frame"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno, hadley/strict"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
m[1, ]
dim(m[1, ])

df <- data.frame(a = 1:3, b = 4:6)
df[, "a"]
df[, c(TRUE, FALSE)]
```
:::

## Why

With `[`, the `drop` argument is `TRUE` by default: as soon as the result has only one row or one column left, R removes the dimension that has become useless. The matrix row becomes a plain vector, with no `dim()`, and the data frame column becomes a vector. A logical index behaves the same way: `df[, c(TRUE, FALSE)]` keeps only `a`, as a vector.

The pitfall shows up in a function written for several columns: the day the filter keeps only one, `nrow()`, `colnames()` or `apply()` receive a vector and fail, or return something else.

## The fix

Write `drop = FALSE` whenever the number of selected rows or columns can fall to one.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
m[1, , drop = FALSE]
df[, "a", drop = FALSE]
```
:::
